subject: Certification gating playbook — control validation & 3P evidence asks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Certification gating playbook — control validation & 3P evidence asks

Team —

We received a tightened ask from Acme Security this morning around what we consider "gating" for certification readiness. They want an explicit playbook that ties control validation artifacts to pass/fail gates for ISO 27001 and our SOC 2 intake (as well as SIG/CAIQ answers). Specifically they asked for: 

- A short list of controls that must be validated before we call the scope "audit-ready" (they called this the "stage gate").
- Owner for each validated artifact and an estimated delivery date.
- Which third-party attestations (e.g., HSM provider, managed IDS) we will accept as evidence vs. those requiring full internal proofs.
- A minimal sampling plan for evidence reviewers (how many instances, services, or days).

Attached I dropped a draft checklist (SIG-Completion-Checklist.xlsx) and a network diagram stub. Can you both take ownership of drafting the gating playbook sections relevant to your areas?

Olga — can you outline the network & boundary validation steps (segmentation diagram + expected logs / retention proof)?
Marissa — can you own the IAM / encryption gating language and catalog any 3P attestations we currently accept?
Rishi — listed as CC for input on sampling approach. Grace — FYI and if you want to adjust owner assignments.

Deliverable: a 1 page playbook + a table mapping control -> artifact -> owner -> target date. Can you aim for an internal draft by EOD Wednesday (2028-04-11)? If any asks require procurement or vendor SLAs, flag them earlier.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Certification gating playbook — control validation & 3P evidence asks

Karthik —

Acknowledged. Quick clarifying questions before I draft the network section: 

1) For FedRAMP alignment (Acme asked about FedRAMP readiness), do they expect P-ATO level artifacts (i.e., SSP excerpts + continuous monitoring outputs) or are they only asking for boundary validation for now? If P-ATO-level, we need to escalate to Product for SSP excerpts.

2) For segmentation evidence: do we provide a single architecture diagram + sample firewall rules, or do they want rule dump exports for the entire edge estate? My preference is a representative sample + a signed attestation from the network owner; that keeps the ask practical.

3) Logging retention: we currently retain infra logs 365 days in S3 (metadata + index). Do we want this to be the gating requirement, or should we propose 180 days for initial audit readiness with a plan to extend?

I'll draft the validation steps and attach the specific artifacts I plan to reference (diagram + export stub + retention table). Targeting Wednesday EOD for a first pass.

- Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: security-ops@acme.com <security-ops@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: auditor@thirdpartyaudit.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Certification gating playbook — control validation & 3P evidence asks

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turn. To be explicit on our end: Acme is looking for a practical gating rubric that lets our internal InfoSec sign off on a scope prior to engaging auditors. We do not need full P-ATO artifacts at this stage, but we do require the following before we mark a scope "audit-ready":

- Ownership confirmations for all control areas (network, IAM, crypto, change mgmt). Owners can be internal (Redwood team) or a named 3P with an attestation and contact.
- Sampled artifacts per control area (for example: 3 firewall rule exports spanning 2 weeks, 5 IAM role change logs, proof of key rotation schedule + one KMS rotation event).
- Evidence of retention and searchable logs for the sampled windows.
- For SIG/CAIQ, a completed questionnaire with direct references to artifacts (we will spot check 15 answers).

On third-party evidence: Acme will accept SOC 2 Type II reports for vendors in place of deeper artifacts, but we will ask for a short attestation that the vendor covers the specific control in scope (e.g., managed secrets or HSM key management).

Sampling guidance: we usually spot-check 10-20% of controls; for cloud infra that equates to the sample sizes above. If you can provide a short table tying sample sizes to control types, that will speed our internal sign-off.

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Security Operations Manager
Acme Financial
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, security-ops@acme.com
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Certification gating playbook — control validation & 3P evidence asks

Thanks Alex — that's exactly the level of detail we wanted. Team, based on Acme's note above let's lock owners and draft the one-page playbook as follows: 

Playbook skeleton (owners assigned):
- Network boundary & segmentation (owner: Olga) — deliverable: annotated diagram + 3 firewall rule exports (target: 2028-04-14)
- IAM & privileged access (owner: Marissa) — deliverable: change log extract + role review evidence + attestation for any managed IAM vendors (target: 2028-04-14)
- Key management & encryption (owner: Marissa) — deliverable: KMS rotation event + policy doc (encryption-policy.pdf) (target: 2028-04-14)
- Logging & retention (owner: Olga) — deliverable: retention table + search demo recording link (target: 2028-04-14)
- Sampling plan (owner: Rishi) — deliverable: table mapping control type -> sample size -> rationale (target: 2028-04-13)

Please attach the artifacts to the Drive folder linked above and add a short note in the SIG checklist column referencing the specific file names. I'll consolidate into the one-page playbook and circulate to Acme for a quick pre-signoff review before we hand to ThirdParty Audit.

If any owner thinks a target date is unrealistic because of procurement or vendor turnaround, flag now so we can escalate.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
